cars.generation: Original centre-tube-chassis C-V8 production-road GT family
cars.specification_market: November 1964 first-hand road-test reference, original 6,276 cc automatic application. The test did not measure acceleration or maximum speed; earlier 5.9-litre figures do not transfer. Native published SAE power is not modern net output. OCR-corrupted bore/compression numbers and gear ratios are omitted. Other marks, engine sizes and later body or gearbox changes add no counts.
cars.summary: The C-V8 paired substantial Chrysler V8 performance with a British four-seat GT body. A contemporary long-distance road test documents its exceptional acceleration and relaxed fast touring, while recording heavy steering and demanding brakes. Its distinct centre-tube chassis and sporting-road identity justify one original family entry, separate from the later FF and Jensen-Healey.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The C-V8 paired substantial Chrysler V8 performance with a British four-seat GT body. A contemporary long-distance road test documents its exceptional acceleration and relaxed fast touring, while recording heavy steering and demanding brakes. Its distinct centre-tube chassis and sporting-road identity justify one original family entry, separate from the later FF and Jensen-Healey.

facts.title: A distinct V8 chassis programme
facts.explanation: The Jensen Museum documents the centre-tube chassis project and its development into the C-V8, supporting its identity as a distinct road-car programme rather than a later FF or Jensen-Healey derivative.

media.caption: Jensen C-V8 photographed by Charles01, file-identified as registered in June 1965 with 6,276 cc. Representative original-family GT body; it is not the November 1964 test car and its present engine, exact mark and originality are not certified by the exterior photograph.
